title: Calibrate Once, Grow the Vocabulary: Candidate-Independent Scores for Conformal Risk Control in Open-Vocabulary Segmentation
abstract: arXiv:2611.20715v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Open-vocabulary segmenters accept class names at inference. Conformal risk control can bound how often their prediction sets miss the true label, but we show that this bound breaks when names are added after calibration. On ADE20K, a threshold calibrated for 10% risk at 150 names reaches up to 15.4% risk at 845 names in released CAT-Seg models. The risk exceeds the target on every calibration split, yet the prediction sets grow far less than the target requires. In SED they instead grow larger than needed. The cause is that pruning, cross-label attention and vocabulary normalisation make each label's score depend on the other requested labels. Scores can move either way, so a threshold recalibrated at a larger vocabulary need not hold at smaller ones. We remove this dependence without training by scoring each label against a fixed reference bank of names. A label's score then stays the same when names are added, so one calibration keeps

translated_title: 一次校准，任意扩展词表：面向开放词汇分割中共形风险控制的候选无关分数
translated_abstract: 开放词汇分割器在推理时可以接受用户输入的类名。共形风险控制可以为其预测集遗漏真实标签的频率提供上界保证，但我们发现，当在校准之后新增类名时，这一保证会被打破。在ADE20K数据集上，已发布的CAT-Seg模型中，针对150个类名以10%风险水平校准的阈值，当类名增加到845个时风险最高可达15.4%。在所有校准划分上风险都超过了目标值，然而预测集的增长却远低于目标所要求的幅度；而在SED模型中，预测集反而增长得比所需的更大。其根本原因在于，剪枝、跨标签注意力以及词表归一化使得每个标签的分数依赖于其他被请求的标签。分数可能向任一方向变化，因此在更大词表上重新校准的阈值在更小词表上未必成立。我们无需任何训练，通过将每个标签与一个固定的参考名称库进行比对来打分，从而消除了这种依赖性。如此一来，当新增类名时，各标签的分数保持不变，因此一次校准即可持续保持有效（摘要原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文揭示了开放词汇分割中共形风险控制在新增类名后失效的问题，并提出一种免训练的候选无关打分方法——将每个标签与固定参考名称库比对，使一次校准即可在任意词表规模下维持有效的风险界限。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that conformal risk control guarantees in open-vocabulary segmentation break when class names are added after calibration, and proposes a training-free, candidate-independent scoring approach based on a fixed reference name bank, so that a single calibration maintains valid risk bounds across arbitrary vocabulary sizes.
